edges.description: Elevated intraocular TGF-beta2 and pro-fibrotic cytokines, alongside infiltrating myeloid cells, drive myofibroblastic transdifferentiation of RPE and stromal/myeloid precursors.
Alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts generated via RPE EMT and myeloid transdifferentiation express vimentin and type I/III collagens to build contractile fibrotic membranes.
ECM deposition and cellular proliferation on the inner and outer retinal surfaces manifest clinically and on OCT as preretinal and subretinal membranes.
Alpha-SMA-mediated myofibroblast contraction within epiretinal and subretinal membranes generates tangential and anteroposterior traction on the retina.
Tangential preretinal and subretinal membrane contraction wrinkles and buckles the retina into high-amplitude corrugations and fixed folds.
Sustained membrane contraction elevates the neurosensory retina off the RPE or causes recurrent postoperative redetachment.
Postoperative epiretinal membrane formation (macular pucker) degrades best-corrected visual acuity even when the retina remains attached.
Unrelieved or recurrent tractional retinal detachment causes severe visual loss and blindness.

nodes.description: Repeated intravitreal or intra-silicone oil injections of methotrexate are used investigatively as an anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative adjunct to vitrectomy for Grade C PVR. In a 74-eye multicenter randomized controlled trial of three 250-microgram intra-silicone oil injections (end of surgery and weeks 3 and 6), methotrexate did not improve overall 6-month retinal reattachment (73.3% vs 76.7%), but significantly reduced limited PVR membrane re-proliferation without redetachment (4.5% vs 39.1%, P = 0.01).

evidence.reference_title: Effects of repeated intra-silicone oil injections of methotrexate on proliferative vitreoretinopathy grade C: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: Retinal reattachment was achieved in 22 eyes (73.3%) in the MTX group and 23 eyes (76.7%) in the control group (difference: -3.4%, 95% CI: -25.2-18.5%).

nodes.description: Combined perioperative 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) has been evaluated as an antiproliferative and anticoagulant/fibrin-binding adjuvant to vitrectomy surgery. Clinical trial results are negative in established disease and conflicting in prophylaxis: an early single-center trial (174 eyes) found reduced postoperative PVR (12.6% vs 26.4%), whereas a multicenter RCT in established Grade C PVR (157 eyes) and the larger 13-center PRIVENT prevention trial (325 eyes) showed no benefit over placebo.

evidence.reference_title: Adjuvant 5-fluorouracil and heparin prevents proliferative vitreoretinopathy : Results from a randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial.
evidence.snippet: The incidence of postoperative PVR was significantly lower (P = 0.02) in the 5-FU and LMWH therapy compared with the placebo group.

evidence.reference_title: A randomized controlled trial of combined 5-fluorouracil and low-molecular-weight heparin in management of established proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: There was no significant difference in success in the primary outcome measure (56%, treatment group; 51%, placebo group; P = 0.59)

evidence.reference_title: Intravitreal 5-Fluorouracil and Heparin to Prevent Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy: Results from a Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: Rate of PVR did not differ between adjuvant therapy with 5-FU and LMWH and placebo treatment in eyes with RRD.

nodes.description: Alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts, dispersed RPE cells, and reactive retinal glial cells (notably Mueller cells) proliferate and deposit dense extracellular matrix enriched in fibronectin (FN1), types I and III collagen (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1), SPARC, and metalloproteinase inhibitors (TIMP1, TIMP3), forming contractile preretinal and subretinal fibrocellular membranes. Vitreous TGF-beta2 levels rise monotonically with clinical fibrosis severity.

evidence.reference_title: Single-Cell Protein and Transcriptional Characterization of Epiretinal Membranes From Patients With Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: Among the former, FN1 (Fibronectin 1), COL1A1 (alpha-1 type I Collagen), COL1A2 (alpha-2 type I Collagen), SPARC (Osteonectin), and COL3A1 (alpha-1 type III Collagen) were the five highest expressed DEG in PVR

evidence.reference_title: Correlation of fibrosis and transforming growth factor-beta type 2 levels in the eye.
evidence.snippet: vitreous aspirates from eyes with intraocular fibrosis associated with PVR have more than three times the amount of TGF-beta

nodes.description: Preretinal (epiretinal/macular pucker) and subretinal fibrocellular membranes (Grade C) are the contractile fibrotic sheets responsible for retinal traction and impaired postoperative visual recovery.

nodes.description: Breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier and retinal tissue injury recruit IBA1- and CD206-positive macrophages and elevate vitreous protein, cytokines, and stromal growth factors including IL-6, IL-1beta, bFGF, HGF, CTGF, and predominantly intraocular TGF-beta2. Elevated vitreous IL-6 and total protein independently predict postoperative PVR development, and infiltrated myeloid cells both amplify pro-fibrotic signaling and contribute directly to the alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblast pool.

evidence.reference_title: Expression of vitreous cytokines in proliferative vitreoretinopathy: a prospective study.
evidence.snippet: The mean levels of TGF-beta2, bFGF, IL-6, and protein in the vitreous were significantly higher (P < 0.05) in patients who had postoperative PVR compared with those who did not.

evidence.reference_title: Expression of vitreous cytokines in proliferative vitreoretinopathy: a prospective study.
evidence.snippet: Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed IL-6 and protein to be significant (P < 0.05), independent, predictive risk factors for the development of PVR.

evidence.reference_title: Novel growth factors involved in the pathogenesis of proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: In each of the five PVR membranes, stromal cells were immunohistochemically positive for both HGF and CTGF.

evidence.reference_title: Single-Cell Protein and Transcriptional Characterization of Epiretinal Membranes From Patients With Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: In line with the sequencing results, we found a strong immunoreactivity for IBA1 and CD206 in PVR membranes when compared to ILM suggesting a role of IBA1/CD206-positive macrophages in the pathogenesis of PVR

nodes.description: Surgical removal of the vitreous, peeling/dissection of contractile epiretinal and subretinal membranes (with relaxing retinotomy/retinectomy when intraretinal foreshortening is present and optional internal limiting membrane peeling to reduce macular pucker), and endotamponade with silicone oil or long-acting gas is the standard and only proven primary management for established PVR, achieving anatomical retinal reattachment in roughly 75-84% of Grade C eyes at 6 months.

evidence.reference_title: A randomized controlled trial of combined 5-fluorouracil and low-molecular-weight heparin in management of established proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: Overall, at 6 months 84% of patients had full retinal reattachment and 94% had stable posterior retinal reattachment.

evidence.reference_title: Effects of repeated intra-silicone oil injections of methotrexate on proliferative vitreoretinopathy grade C: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: Retinal reattachment was achieved in 45 eyes (75.0%) at 6 months after surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy: A Review.
evidence.snippet: At this time, surgery is the only management option for PVR as there is no proven pharmacologic agent for the treatment or prevention of PVR.

nodes.description: Dispersed RPE cells lose epithelial cell-cell junctions and undergo epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) into matrix-producing, contractile alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblast-like cells under activated vitreous TGF-beta and CTGF signaling, complemented by myeloid-to-myofibroblast transdifferentiation within developing PVR membranes.

evidence.reference_title: Single-Cell Protein and Transcriptional Characterization of Epiretinal Membranes From Patients With Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: TYRP1-expression was observed in one out of five stained PVR membranes and colocalized with α-SMA pointing toward a possible epithelial-to-mesenchymal transdifferentiation of RPE cells to myofibroblasts in this patient

evidence.reference_title: Novel growth factors involved in the pathogenesis of proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: The TGF-beta is activated, upregulating expression of CTGF. Under the influence of TGF-beta and CTGF, RPE become myofibroblastic and fibrosis ensues.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms of epithelial-mesenchymal transition in proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: RPE cells undergo a process named epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), by which differentiated epithelial cells go through a phenotypic conversion that gives rise to the matrix-producing fibroblasts and myofibroblasts

nodes.description: A full-thickness retinal break, detachment, or surgical/traumatic injury breaches the neurosensory retina, blood-retinal barrier, and retinal pigment epithelial monolayer. RPE cells lose contact with Bruch's membrane and disperse into the vitreous cavity and subretinal space, where local injury triggers a dysregulated wound-healing response with HGF-associated migration of RPE cell clusters.

nodes.description: Contraction of preretinal, intraretinal, and subretinal fibrocellular membranes distorts retinal lamellar architecture, producing outer retinal corrugations, fixed retinal folds, retinal foreshortening, and tractional (re)detachment. Severity is staged clinically by the 1991 Retina Society classification (Grades A-C, subdivided into posterior and anterior contraction types by clock-hour extent).

evidence.reference_title: An updated classification of retinal detachment with proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
evidence.snippet: A more detailed description of posterior and anterior contractions has been made possible by adding contraction types such as focal, diffuse, subretinal, circumferential contraction, and anterior displacement.

evidence.reference_title: Assessment of Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy in Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment with OCT: Revisiting the 1991 Retina Society Classification.
evidence.snippet: Significant preretinal membranes with loss of differentiation of the inner and outer retinal lamellae and distortion of underlying ORCs were observed.

nodes.description: Membrane contraction produces tangential and anteroposterior traction on the retina, leading to tractional (re)detachment, the end-stage anatomic outcome of PVR and the primary cause of failed retinal reattachment surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Correlation of fibrosis and transforming growth factor-beta type 2 levels in the eye.
evidence.snippet: Approximately 1 out of every 10 eyes undergoing surgery for retinal detachment develops excessive intraocular fibrosis that can lead to traction retinal detachment and ultimate blindness.

evidence.snippet: those patients in whom postoperative PVR developed tended to have poorer vision (P < 0.0001).

nodes.description: Vitreous haze, pigment clumps, and pigment clusters on the inferior retina (Grade A) are the earliest clinical signs of PVR, reflecting dispersed RPE cells, proteinaceous exudate, and inflammatory cells in the vitreous cavity.
